title: 1 Kings 6
paragraphs: ¹ In the four hundred and eightieth year after the Israelites came out of Egypt — in the fourth year of Solomon's reign over Israel, in the month of Ziv, the second month — he began to build the temple of the LORD. ² The temple King Solomon built for the LORD was sixty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high. ³ The portico at the front of the main hall was twenty cubits wide, matching the width of the temple, and extended ten cubits out from the front. ⁴ He made narrow clerestory windows in the temple. ⁵ Against the walls of the main hall and the inner sanctuary he built a structure around the temple, in which there were side rooms:

⁶ The lowest floor of the side rooms was five cubits wide, the middle floor was six cubits wide, and the third floor was seven cubits wide. The temple had a ledge built around the outside so that the beams of the side rooms would not be set into the walls. ⁷ In building the temple, only blocks dressed at the quarry were used, and no hammer, chisel, or any other iron tool was heard at the temple site while it was being built. ⁸ The entrance to the lowest floor was on the south side of the temple. A stairway led up to the middle level and then to the third. ⁹ So he built the temple and completed it, roofing it with beams and cedar planks. ¹⁰ He built the side rooms all along the temple — each room five cubits high, attached to the temple by cedar beams.

¹¹ The word of the LORD came to Solomon: ¹² "As for this temple you are building — if you follow my decrees, observe my laws, and keep all my commands and obey them, I will fulfill through you the promise I gave to your father David. ¹³ I will live among the Israelites and will not abandon my people Israel." ¹⁴ So Solomon built the temple and completed it. ¹⁵ He lined the interior walls of the temple with cedar boards, paneling them from the floor to the ceiling. He covered the floor with planks of pine.

¹⁶ He partitioned off twenty cubits at the rear of the temple with cedar boards from floor to ceiling to form within the temple an inner sanctuary, the Most Holy Place. ¹⁷ The main hall in front of this room was forty cubits long. ¹⁸ The cedar of the interior was carved with gourds and open flowers. Everything was cedar; no stone was visible. ¹⁹ He prepared the inner sanctuary within the temple to set the ark of the covenant of the LORD there. ²⁰ The inner sanctuary was twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high. He overlaid the inside with pure gold, and he also overlaid the cedar altar.

²¹ Solomon overlaid the inside of the temple with pure gold, and he extended gold chains across the front of the inner sanctuary, which was overlaid with gold. ²² He overlaid the whole interior with gold. He also overlaid with gold the altar belonging to the inner sanctuary. ²³ For the inner sanctuary he made two cherubim out of olive wood, each ten cubits high. ²⁴ One wing of the first cherub was five cubits long, and the other wing was also five cubits — ten cubits from the tip of one wing to the tip of the other. ²⁵ The second cherub also measured ten cubits: both cherubim were identical in size and shape.

²⁶ Each cherub stood ten cubits tall. ²⁷ Solomon placed the cherubim inside the inner sanctuary, and they spread their wings so that one wing of the first cherub touched one wall while a wing of the second cherub touched the opposite wall — and their inner wings touched each other in the middle of the room. ²⁸ He overlaid the cherubim with gold. ²⁹ He carved the walls of the entire house with figures of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers — all the way around, inside and out. ³⁰ He covered the floors with gold, inside and out.

³¹ For the entrance to the inner sanctuary he made doors of olive wood; the lintel and doorposts were a fifth of the wall's width. ³² Both doors were olive wood, and he carved cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers on them, then overlaid them with gold, hammering the gold onto the cherubim and the palm trees. ³³ He made the same for the doorposts of the main hall — olive wood, a quarter of the wall's width. ³⁴ The two doors themselves were of cypress wood, each door having two folding leaves. ³⁵ He carved cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers on them and covered them with gold laid evenly over the carved work.

³⁶ He built the inner courtyard with three courses of dressed stone and one course of cedar beams. ³⁷ The foundation of the LORD's house had been laid in the fourth year, in the month of Ziv. ³⁸ In the eleventh year, in the month of Bul — the eighth month — the house was finished in every detail, exactly as it had been designed. Solomon had spent seven years building it.
